title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 8 vs. Dallas Cowboys
headline: Cardinals won in OT despite a wave of injuries (Love, Knight, Bourne, J. Williams, Virgil). LaFleur benched Brissett for Minshew midgame and wouldn't commit to a Week 9 starter.
summary: LaFleur opened by listing five in-game injuries: Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Bam Knight (neck), Kendrick Bourne (ankle), Jayden Williams (knee) and Reggie Virgil (low back). None returned, and he said he'd know more tomorrow once the team is back home. He said Love was never ruled out but he wasn't aware of any chance he'd return. He pulled Jacoby Brissett for Gardner Minshew because the offense needed a spark, and he took the blame as a collective failure of scheme and play calling. When asked whether Minshew starts next week, he dodged and said he was just excited about the win. He credited Minshew's timing and readiness, and said a six-yard completion to Devin Duvernay and a long run unlocked the offense. Josh Fryar replaced Jayden Williams at left tackle and drew praise, and LaFleur said he still trusts Williams. By the end the offense was down to one running back, and LaFleur said he was calling plays by formation because he barely knew who was available. Michael Wilson played through visible pain for 100+ yards and two touchdowns. LaFleur also said he trusts L.J. Collier after an unnecessary-roughness penalty and praised Josh Sweat, and he credited the defense for holding Dallas to 3.6 yards per play.

injuries.detail: Ankle injury, did not return. LaFleur said he was never ruled out but wasn't aware of any chance he'd come back. More info expected tomorrow.
Neck injury, did not return. Severity unknown, and LaFleur said he'd know more tomorrow.
Ankle injury, did not return. Severity not given.
Knee injury, did not return. Josh Fryar replaced him at left tackle.
Low back injury, did not return. Severity not given.

signals.note: He sparked the offense in the second half and is a live QB1 candidate, but LaFleur wouldn't confirm a starter.
signals.quote: he's ready at all times.

signals.note: He is the lead back, so his Week 9 availability is the key fantasy question.

signals.note: With Love also hurt, the backfield is thin and Knight's status matters for RB depth.

signals.note: If Love and Knight miss time, he is in line for a large workload.

signals.note: WR depth is already depleted, so his status affects target distribution.

signals.note: Another pass-catcher whose status will shape WR snaps and targets.

signals.claim: Williams left with a knee injury and did not return; LaFleur still has a lot of trust in him long-term.
signals.note: His absence affects the left tackle spot and pass protection.

signals.claim: Fryar filled in at left tackle when Williams went down and will keep that role if Williams is out.
signals.note: The offense looked better with him in, and he may start at LT if Williams misses time.
signals.quote: I have a lot of trust in fryer and I know they do too.

signals.note: He is a clear target-getter with the WR group depleted, though his own health bears watching.

topics.detail: LaFleur took responsibility, saying he needs to be better with scheme and play calling. He said the offense needs to execute for 60 minutes rather than only the final 30.
The defense held Dallas to 3.6 yards per play, and LaFleur praised Nick's game plan and the defenders' focus.
L.J. Collier took an unnecessary-roughness penalty and LaFleur said he trusts him not to repeat it. He also pulled Josh Sweat aside for yelling at Collier but praised Sweat's play and growth.
The kicker (Chad) missed an extra point but came back to deliver in overtime, and LaFleur called the team resilient.
The team ended with three receivers, a running back and a tackle hurt. LaFleur called it the most extreme skill-position injury situation he has seen and said he was calling plays by formation.

title: Kevin Stefanski on Atlanta Falcons performance against Tampa Bay Buccaneers | Press Conference
headline: Falcons lose a wet-weather game to Tampa Bay (Bucs ran for 324 yards); Samson Ebukam and Zachariah Branch both have hamstring injuries pending imaging, and Stefanski says he has no concerns about Michael Penix Jr. after a shaky game.
summary: Stefanski opened by announcing hamstring injuries to Samson Ebukam and Zachariah Branch, with imaging to come and more information later. He said the team did not do a good enough job in a game played in wet conditions that both sides had to deal with, and he credited Tampa Bay's players and coaches for outplaying and outcoaching Atlanta. Asked about Michael Penix Jr. looking shaky after a big game the week before, he said he has no concerns, that everyone including himself can do better, and that the wet ball was a factor in the passing struggles. On the run defense that allowed 324 yards, he credited the Buccaneers' scheme and blocking and said it comes down to discipline, tackling, and looking at what schematic help the defense can be given. He acknowledged the offense failed to stay on the field on third down and in short yardage. His message to the team was to own the result and move on. He gave no specifics on lineup or role changes.

injuries.detail: Hamstring injury; imaging to be done, more information to come.
Hamstring injury; imaging to be done, more information to come.

signals.claim: Penix remains the starting quarterback; the coach has no concerns after the poor game.
signals.note: The coach blamed the wet ball and shared responsibility rather than signaling a change, but a poor outing following a big game makes him a volatile start.

signals.claim: Branch has a hamstring injury and will undergo imaging to determine severity.
signals.note: A hamstring injury puts his availability for next week in doubt, which affects his return and receiving usage.
signals.quote: Zachariah branch. Hamstring injuries. We'll do some imaging on those.

signals.claim: Ebukam has a hamstring injury and will undergo imaging to determine severity.
signals.note: A hamstring injury puts his availability at risk, which matters for Atlanta's pass-rush rotation and IDP value.
signals.quote: Samson. Ebukam. Zachariah branch. Hamstring injuries. We'll do some imaging on those.

topics.detail: Tampa Bay ran for 324 yards. Stefanski credited their scheme and blocking, called run defense a matter of discipline and tackling, and said the staff will look at what schematic help it can give the defense.
Stefanski pointed to the rain and wet ball as factors that affected both teams. He admitted the offense failed to stay on the field on third down and in short yardage.
He said the team will own the loss and move on, and that Tampa Bay outplayed and outcoached Atlanta.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Week 8 Loss to Bills
headline: Lamar Jackson is headed to IR with a surgery-level injury after going down on the first play. Tyler Huntley also got hurt, which leaves Joe Fagnano as the likely Thursday QB.
summary: Minter said Baltimore lost Lamar Jackson on the first play of the 36-10 loss at Buffalo. He said Jackson will need surgery and go to IR, but he would not say whether that means season-ending or define the injury. Backup Tyler Huntley ("Snoop") also left the game, and his status is unknown. Joe Fagnano came in with few reps in preparation, hung in there and did some good things, and Minter praised him and said the team believes in him. The defense played well early with turnovers and red-zone stops. It later gave up big plays while reaching for splash plays, let Buffalo off the hook on a couple of fourth downs, and gave up 4-5 yard runs. Minter called the offensive line a tough evaluation because the game plan was built around a starting QB who went down immediately. The team plays Thursday on a short week after the defense logged a ton of snaps. Minter said Baltimore will figure out its QB depth over the next 24 hours, depending on Huntley's status and whether Fagnano came through the game healthy.

injuries.detail: Injured on the first play. Minter said he will need surgery and go to IR, but would not say whether it is season-ending or define the injury.
Left the game after replacing Jackson. Minter said he was unsure of his status going forward and that it would be checked over the next 24 hours.

signals.claim: Jackson will have surgery and be placed on injured reserve, so he will miss at least the next several games, including Thursday.
signals.note: Baltimore's QB1 is out for an unspecified, possibly season-long stretch, which hurts the whole Ravens offense.
signals.quote: That'll be a surgery deal. He'll go to IR.

signals.claim: Huntley's availability for Thursday will be determined within the next 24 hours.
signals.note: If he can't play, Baltimore may have to add another QB. That would affect who starts on Thursday.
signals.quote: Yeah, I'm not sure of that yet. We'll see.

signals.claim: Fagnano is a candidate to start at QB on Thursday, depending on Huntley's status.
signals.note: He may become the starting QB on a short week, which would shape the outlook for Baltimore's pass catchers.
signals.quote: If it's Joe, we got a lot of belief in Joe

topics.detail: The defense kept the game close early with turnovers and red-zone stops. It later gave up big plays after reaching for splash plays, let Buffalo convert fourth downs, and allowed 4-5 yard runs.
Minter called it a tough evaluation after many pressures and sacks, since the game plan changed once the starting QB went down. The film still needs to be reviewed.
Baltimore plays Thursday after the defense played a ton of snaps. Minter's focus is keeping the team together, recovering and putting in a good plan.

Asked about an emergency QB (Justice Hill was named by a reporter), Minter did not confirm a plan. He said it depends on who can run a functioning offense and that the QB situation will be sorted out within 24 hours.

title: Joe Brady Talks Josh Allen Breaking A Franchise Record In Victory Over The Ravens
headline: DJ Moore is back and healthy, and Brady called him a big part of the offense. Spencer Brown missed the game and Bobby Graves started at tackle. Ed Oliver returned to a defense built around him.
summary: Brady was thrilled with the defense in the 36-10 win over Baltimore. He praised the pressure, the communication and the effort, and said the standard holds no matter who plays quarterback for the opponent. He was angry at halftime about the offense, citing turnovers and penalties that he called "Groundhog Day," and said the second half looked more like the standard. Josh Allen passed Jim Kelly for the franchise touchdown record, and Brady called him incredible. DJ Moore returned, made big plays, and Brady said he is good to go and changes how defenses play Buffalo, though Allen wanted one more deep shot to him. Ed Oliver also returned, and Brady said the defense was built around him whether or not he makes the play. Spencer Brown was held out; the decision came the night before because he did not feel his best, and Bobby Graves started and played well. Brady had no update on Josh Palmer. He also expressed strong confidence in kicker Tyler Bass, said he takes the blame for the failed fourth-and-one, and explained his end-of-half timeout. On whether Damar Hamlin keeps his starting spot, he said it's too early to say.

injuries.detail: Held out. Brady said he wasn't feeling like the best version of himself, and the call was made the night before. Brady said Brown was close, and that he had to protect him from himself. No timeline was given.
Returned to action and made big plays. Brady said he gets hit hard every time but is good to go.
Back on the field after an absence. Brady praised his hits on the quarterback and his involvement.
Asked for an update, Brady said he had none.

signals.note: Moore's return restores a key target and changes how defenses play Buffalo, which is good for his and Allen's fantasy value.

signals.note: Allen remains a premier fantasy QB, and Brady said he can't be game-planned for.

signals.note: The defense is built around him, which is a plus for Buffalo IDP and team defense value.
signals.quote: we built this defense around it.

signals.note: His starting role is unsettled, which matters to IDP owners.
signals.quote: I think it's too early to kind of get a get a feel from that.

signals.note: With no update from Brady, his availability remains uncertain, and it matters for WR depth.

signals.note: Brady's confidence is a plus for Bass's value as a kicker on a high-scoring team.
signals.quote: He's going to continue to make big kicks for us.

topics.detail: Brady was angry about turnovers and penalties, including in the red zone, and called it "Groundhog Day." He said the second half was more like the standard but wants cleaner execution.

The defense played well all game, with strong communication and pressure. Brady praised the blitz calls by the defensive coordinator and said blitzing is also about creating matchups, not just getting home.

Bobby Graves played well in place of Spencer Brown, and Brady said he won't have to call the game differently with Graves in. Brady also said backups like Graves and T. Couch are ready when called on.
Brady said the failed fourth-and-one was on him and that Baltimore did nothing different.
Brady explained the late first-half timeout as a way to get into field goal range without giving Baltimore the ball back. He said he may feel differently after film.

title: Zac Taylor Recaps Overtime Win Over Titans | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Cincinnati beat Tennessee in overtime to reach 5-2. Chase and Higgins got the ball in overtime, Burrow scored six TDs with three INTs, and Dexter Lawrence sealed the game with a sack.
summary: Taylor stressed that the Bengals found a way to win a game that went against them early. They fell behind 13-0 after a slow start against Tennessee's tempo, and the offense never found a rhythm in the first quarter. The team turned the ball over four times, including three Burrow interceptions, one of them a double move against quarters that the safety jumped. Tennessee switched to more one-high looks and tighter coverage, so Cincinnati needed a series to adjust. After that the offense found a rhythm late in regulation and in overtime, scoring two touchdowns with short throws that Chase and Higgins turned into chunk plays. Dexter Lawrence got the final defensive stop with a sack, and Taylor said that is why you trade for a player like him. Taylor said Mike Gesicki is always ready when his moment comes, though he had only one catch through three quarters. Cashius Howell's injury was described as a wrist, Taylor could not recall the DJ update and promised more Wednesday, and the team travels to Spain on Tuesday night.

injuries.detail: Taylor thought it was his wrist but gave no status and said he would update on Wednesday.

injuries.player: DJ (unidentified; possibly DJ Turner or DJ Ivey)
injuries.detail: Taylor said he was just told about it, could not remember the details and promised an update Wednesday.

signals.claim: Chase will remain a primary target, getting chunk plays on short throws, as he did in overtime.
signals.note: Overtime showed the team leaning on Chase when the game was on the line; his emotion on the sideline did not worry Taylor.
signals.quote: I trust him to do his job through all circumstances.

signals.claim: Higgins will keep getting featured, including on deep slants against outside leverage.
signals.note: He was a main target late in regulation and in overtime, and the deep slant at the end of the fourth quarter was a big play.
signals.quote: And those guys just turned them into bigger plays.

signals.claim: The three interceptions will be reviewed and cleaned up on film.
signals.note: He scored six total touchdowns and was praised for escaping pressure, but the three INTs add some volatility.
signals.quote: he stepped up in those big moments for us.

signals.claim: Gesicki can produce bursts of catches late in games when defenses take other players away.
signals.note: His role is situational and reliable, with big-moment catches and a touchdown; he had only one catch through three quarters.
signals.quote: he's always ready for the ball to come his way

signals.claim: Lawrence is an impact player on the defensive line.
signals.note: He ended the game with a sack, which helps IDP value, and Taylor said the trade is paying off.
signals.quote: he stepped up and been the impact player we hoped he would be.

signals.note: Hill came out of the game in the first and second quarters, which surprised people. Taylor praised him but did not explain why.
signals.quote: Whatever we ask him to do, he's a total professional.

topics.detail: Cincinnati fell behind 13-0 against Tennessee's tempo and committed four turnovers. Taylor said they will study the film, and he thought the team's urgency was fine.
Tennessee played tighter coverage and more one-high looks than the two-high looks Cincinnati used last week, and it pressured Burrow. Cincinnati needed a series to adjust.
Tony Pollard had early success with Tennessee's tempo. Taylor did not have a clear explanation and said he would study the film.
Taylor said the trade doesn't change game planning much, because teams already slide their protection to the best interior rusher. It just means the team can plan around that.
The team flies to Spain on Tuesday night, so the early part of the week is sped up.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Steelers : November 1st, 2026
headline: Browns' offense and run defense both collapsed in a 27-6 loss to Pittsburgh; Monken stuck with Deshaun Watson through heavy pressure, and Carson Schwesinger is playing through an ankle injury (the other one this time).
summary: Monken took ownership of the 27-6 divisional loss, saying the team didn't start fast, committed two early turnovers, went three-and-out repeatedly, took too many penalties and sacks, and never got the run game going. He said Pittsburgh hurt the defense with schemed runs, including a roughly 50-yard trap play on third-and-13, and that missed tackles in open space against two hard-running backs made it worse. On protection, he said the sack problem is a recurring issue that has to be fixed through better scheme, blocking and getting receivers open, and that Pittsburgh's pass rushers and blitzes were effective. He said he never considered pulling Deshaun Watson late despite the beating, because he wanted to see him keep playing and battle. He rejected youth as an excuse and said it was a coaching and playing failure. He praised Carson Schwesinger as a tough warrior playing through an ankle injury, noting it is the other ankle and that he wasn't sure Schwesinger would play a couple of weeks ago. He also backed the kicker after two missed kicks, calling him elite after a streak of 24-25 makes. The Browns are 5-3 and next face the Saints coming off their bye.

injuries.detail: Playing through an ankle injury, now the opposite ankle from before. Monken didn't think he'd play a couple of weeks ago but he did, and called him an 'absolute stud'.
Monken cited him as an example of a player who returned against Pittsburgh earlier, played well, then missed three more weeks. This was a past reference, not a current status.

signals.claim: Watson stays the starting QB and was not considered for benching despite taking heavy pressure.
signals.note: His job looks safe for now, but the protection problems and sack volume put his fantasy floor at risk against good pass rushes.
signals.quote: I want to see him continue to play and battle.

signals.claim: Pass protection and the scheme must improve after too many sacks; the issue has recurred over multiple games.
signals.note: Repeated sack problems hurt the passing game's efficiency and Watson's fantasy outlook until fixed.

signals.claim: Schwesinger will keep playing through an ankle injury, though his health is worth monitoring.
signals.note: The IDP-relevant linebacker is playing hurt on the other ankle, so a missed game is possible.
signals.quote: He's an absolute stud absolute warrior.

topics.detail: Pittsburgh gained big yardage on schemed runs such as traps and edge plays, including a ~50-yard run on third-and-13. Missed tackles in space against two physical backs added to it. Monken said the run defense must be fixed and that similar problems showed up against Tennessee the week before.
Two turnovers on the first two drives, repeated three-and-outs, ten penalties, many sacks and no run game. Monken said that to fix it, the team has to improve protection and other areas on offense.
Monken backed the kicker after two misses, noting a streak of about 24-25 straight makes, and called him one of the best kickers in the NFL.
Monken rejected the 'young team' excuse and said the Browns earned their 5-3 record. He said he isn't worried about the team bouncing back and will review the tape and reset.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 8 #AZvsDAL
headline: Cowboys blew a 14-3 halftime lead in a 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona; Caleb Downs is in concussion protocol, and Joey Porter Jr. and Jake Ferguson both have ankle injuries that need more testing.
summary: Schottenheimer called it a tale of two halves. Dallas led 14-3 at halftime, then failed to finish in all three phases: the defense couldn't get stops, the offense didn't close out in the four-minute situation, and the team didn't score enough in the red zone. He said he doesn't think his play calling was too conservative, though he wants to review the film. He said Dallas wanted to get the run game going, and Arizona stuffed it, tipped passes at the line and mixed coverages. A big play to George Pickens was called back by penalty, and another was lost to a penalty. Arizona's second-half run game, led by big back Algiers, produced explosive plays, and Mitch Minshew's entry at quarterback gave them a spark. On injuries, Caleb Downs is in the concussion protocol, P.J. Locke's status is unclear, and Joey Porter Jr. and Jake Ferguson have ankle injuries that will get more testing. He publicly backed Dak Prescott, Shemar James and Quinnen Williams, said he owns his part of the loss, and said there is plenty of football left.

title: Campbell on Week 8 performance
headline: Lions won a gritty Week 8 game over Minnesota by running for 230 yards, but LB Jack Campbell's injury is serious and unresolved, and several other starters (Wonnum, Cade Mays, 'BB') were hurt and may miss time.
summary: Dan Campbell opened by saying the team's thoughts are with Jack Campbell, who is being cared for, and that there is no new information yet. He called the win over a top-tier Vikings defense a tough, gritty one that needed defense and special teams to play well first. The offense then had to close it out, and the run game was the key. Detroit finished with about 230 rushing yards, with the run game stronger in the second half and fourth quarter than in the first. He said the Vikings pressure and move a lot, so early on the line's combination blocks, footwork and targets were a bit off. The Lions put a heavy, high-volume run load on the O-line and Jared Goff, with new wrinkles, and the unit settled in. He praised the O-line, tight ends, Gibbs, receivers blocking downfield and the play calling, and said an unnamed back who had been challenged to produce carries and pass protect took a big step and earned trust. Defense lost four or five starters during the game, forcing position moves, including Derrick Barnes shifting over and Malcolm Rodriguez coming in, and Campbell was proud of how they handled it. On injuries, he said Wonnum, Cade Mays and 'BB' were hurt, none seem long-term, but a week or two or more is possible, and he had little information.

injuries.detail: Injured in the game after a long stoppage; he is being taken care of and the team has no new information, with updates to come.
Hurt in the game. Campbell doesn't think it's long-term but could be out a week or two or more; no firm info.
Hurt in the game. Campbell doesn't think it's long-term but said he doesn't know about next week.
Referred to only as 'BB', so Brian Branch and Ben Bartch are both possible. Hurt in the game; not seen as long-term but could miss a week or two or more.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts at Jaguars postgame
headline: Colts got blown out 42-7 by Jacksonville; Steichen says every position is up for evaluation, with Daniel Jones' starting job not clearly endorsed and Jonathan Taylor limited to 8 carries by game script.
summary: Steichen opened by saying the Colts were outplayed and outcoached in all three phases in the 42-7 loss at Jacksonville, and he accepted blame as head coach. He said the locker room had energy but it never showed on the field, and he called for better effort and tackling after a lot of missed arm tackles. Asked whether the trades of Clinton and another player sapped the team's energy, he said players must stay professional and the next man has to step up. He praised rookie Caden Curry for his effort, including on special teams. Asked about pulling Daniel Jones late, he said the team was down so many scores that DJ Giddens and Anthony Richardson got late reps. When pressed on Jones as the starter, he only said he will evaluate every position going forward, without a clear endorsement. He said Jonathan Taylor's eight carries were purely a product of game flow and not a planned number, and he credited Josh Downs for being a pro after a trade request and making a couple of catches. He declined to address his job security and said everything, including possible lineup changes, will be evaluated after this game.

signals.claim: Jones' starting QB job will be evaluated along with every other position going forward.
signals.note: Steichen declined to commit to Jones as the starter after he was pulled late, which adds risk to his fantasy value.
signals.quote: I'm going to evaluate everything every position going forward.

signals.quote: Anthony got in there, got some reps there at the end.

signals.note: The workload dip should be temporary and volume should rebound in a more competitive game.

signals.claim: Downs remains active and productive despite his trade request.
signals.note: Steichen praised his professionalism, suggesting no punishment for the trade request, though his future with the team is still uncertain.

He said everything will be evaluated after this game, including possible lineup changes, and effort shown on tape will matter.

Asked about recent trades, he said the team must stay professional and the next player must step up.

title: Liam Coen Recaps Decisive Win Over the Colts in Week 8 | Press Conference
headline: Bhayshul Tuten ran for his first career 100-yard game in the 42-7 win, but DaVon Hamilton's injury looks serious and the safety group and O-line (Ezra Cleveland) are banged up.
summary: Coen was pleased with a fast start: a 98-yard opening touchdown drive that mixed in the run, an explosive play to Brenton Strange and a Trevor Lawrence touchdown throw in the back of the end zone. He praised the run game, especially Bhayshul Tuten, who was more patient, ran through contact and had a great week of practice. Chris Rodriguez Jr. and Ameer Abdullah also ran hard, and the line stayed connected to blocks longer. Wyatt Milum filled in for Ezra Cleveland and helped open holes on some long runs. Second-year special-teamer Rayuan Lane had a game-breaking interception returned for a touchdown. The secondary needed next-man-up play because Antonio Johnson did not play and Eric Murray got nicked up, and Kaevon Merriweather and others stepped in. Coen called DaVon Hamilton's injury extremely difficult and said the team has to evaluate how serious it is. He also praised Lawrence's off-schedule play and a long throw to Nate Boerkircher on a half-roll bootleg, though he was disappointed in the sacks that stalled some drives and a low red zone penalty.

Wyatt Milum stepped in for him, which implies he was out or left the game. No details were given.

title: Klint Kubiak Postgame Presser - 11.1.26 | Week 8
headline: Mike Washington Jr. got an expanded early-down role while Ashton Jeanty had only two carries by Kubiak's call, and Jalen Nailor and both tight ends (Bowers and Mayer) produced.
summary: Kubiak opened by saying player #26 left with a groin injury and will be evaluated tomorrow. He praised the fans and called the win resilient, if not pretty. He said Ashton Jeanty's two carries were his own decision, unrelated to Jeanty's earlier comments. He wanted to give Mike Washington Jr. more opportunities, and he called Jeanty a big part of the run and pass game going forward. Washington ran hard and was a step forward for the run game, but how the backfield splits will depend on film and matchup, and Kubiak said he trusts both runners. He praised Jalen Nailor for making the most of his chances after working hard without opportunities. He said Kirk Cousins has been a leader and playmaker all year, and he credited tight ends coach Luke Steckel as Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer combined for about 12 catches and 130 yards. Defensively, the run defense keeps starting games poorly and is something the coaches must fix. Kubiak liked the third-down success, which came from protection, receivers getting open and Cousins distributing the ball, but he wants better first and second downs.

injuries.detail: Suffered a groin injury in the game; the team will take a look at him tomorrow.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Loss in Detroit vs. the Lions, Injury Updates & Kyler Murray
headline: Vikings lost at Detroit; Kyler Murray (hamstring tightness) returned and is fine, Justin Jefferson was targeted 9 times but frustrated, and KOC promises to keep finding ways to get him the ball ahead of Monday Night Football.
summary: O'Connell opened by sending thoughts to Lions' Jack Campbell, who was hurt in the game, then called the loss the team's first real adversity and said the Vikings must respond quickly. He said the team battled and made plays, but left too many on the field, especially in the passing game, where negative plays and three-and-outs created third-and-longs. He did not fault Justin Jefferson's frustration, noting there were missed chances to get him the ball in a 50-play game, and said the staff will keep finding ways to feed him. On Kyler Murray, he praised some big throws but said the offense needs more consistent completions and rhythm, and he pointed to gun run, play action, screens and movement concepts that suit Murray. He explained going for it on fourth-and-four, where he said J.A. (Jauan Jennings?) was in a one-on-one matchup; the deep shot was forced up early by pressure. He also said he trusted the defense when he punted late, and the defense then gave up the game-winning drive. He said the run game faced tough sledding against Detroit's base defense versus 11 personnel, though Murray's runs helped. Injuries: Theo Jackson (quad contusion) did not return; O'Neill cleared concussion eval; Rodgers has an ankle sprain; Bredeson returned from a knee evaluation; Murray returned late. Next up is Monday Night Football at U.S. Bank Stadium.

title: Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (11/1) | Week 8
headline: Braelon Allen ran for close to 150 yards in Breece Hall's absence, and Hall and David Bailey were both 'close' to playing but are being held back to avoid a setback.
summary: Glenn was disappointed after a close Week 8 loss in which the Jets scored on their first six possessions. He praised the offense for moving the ball, running well, and producing explosive plays, and said Garrett Wilson and another player (likely a skill player, name unclear in the captions) were involved. He blamed the defense for giving up too many points, along with special teams for allowing a kickoff return touchdown and critical third-down penalties. He also pointed to red-zone struggles on both sides: roughly 2-for-5 or 2-for-6 on offense, with the opponent scoring every time on defense. Glenn took responsibility as the play caller for not getting the defense into the right calls, especially against a team he knew would run the ball. He said five of the team's losses have come by a score or less, but stressed the team plays hard and has no quit. On injuries, he said several players had nicks but returned to the game, and he promised an update on any true injuries later. Breece Hall was close to playing and Braelon Allen did a great job with nearly 150 yards. Hall and David Bailey are both being handled carefully to avoid setbacks.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Browns
headline: Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle are both 'hitting their stride' and McCarthy wants each to touch the ball every week, with the run game a focal point behind a rising offensive line.
summary: McCarthy was upbeat after the 27-6 division win over the Browns, Pittsburgh's fourth straight, which moved the team to 6-2 heading into the bye. He said the run defense has set a high bar over the past two weeks and that running the ball was a focal point that the team accomplished. He praised both running backs, saying Jaylen Warren is 'on fire' and Rico Dowdle is also playing well, and that it is important for both to touch the ball every week. He credited Aaron Rodgers with calling the goal-line play before halftime, a Nittany package touchdown to Pat Freiermuth, and called Zach Frazier a special, unique player. McCarthy admitted the offense should have scored more and that he wishes he could have the three red-zone plays back, where the team came up short near the goal line. He said the staff is only starting to work through its menu of schemes, and that traps, which they haven't used much, were a good fit against Cleveland. He praised Patrick Queen's play and the intensity of the front seven. Looking ahead, he wants the team to come off the bye healthy before a three-game stretch with two road games and a home game on the Friday after Thanksgiving.

signals.note: McCarthy singled him out as the hotter back and said the team can't get him the ball enough, which supports a steady workload.

Pittsburgh is 6-2 and heads into the bye hoping to come out healthy. After it comes a three-game stretch with two road games and then a home game on the Friday after Thanksgiving.

title: Todd Bowles Discusses Historic Victory vs. Falcons | Press Conference
headline: Bucs ran for big yardage in a rainy 4-INT win over Atlanta; Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell both ran well, and Bowles says the team is gelling at 3-5.
summary: Bowles described a nasty, rainy and windy game in which ball security was the priority, and he said the conditions, not the game plan, kept the passing game from doing anything. The Bucs leaned on the ground game for the second straight week, with Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell doing the heavy lifting behind an offensive line that he said is improving. Gainwell went over 100 yards, and Bowles praised both backs for the "yeoman's work" they have been doing. He singled out Alex Anzalone for setting the tone with two early plays and said he is growing more comfortable in the defense. He also praised Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish as sticky cover players who make plays every week. Baker Mayfield threw only about 14 times over two weeks, but Bowles credited him with great quarterback play, including checks and blitz recognition. Bowles said the team is still 3-5 and has "a lot more digging to do," and that the offensive line and coaches are figuring out which runs fit the players. He was still unhappy with a late pass play where two defenders could have made a play and didn't.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cam Ward topped 300 passing yards in a 36-point effort, and Saleh praised the tempo; Amani Hooker is playing at a Pro Bowl level, and Marcus Harris and James Williams are injury checks after the Week 8 loss at Cincinnati.
summary: Saleh said Tennessee lost another close game, the sixth this season, because the team can't close out the last five minutes, even though the players fought hard. The Titans played a "feast or famine" defensive plan against Cincinnati's explosive offense, forcing four takeaways (the defense had three interceptions) but giving up some big plays. He called the offense outstanding and said the tempo helps Cam Ward. He thought the receivers made plays after the catch and that Daboll and his staff schemed guys open. The final drive stalled about 15 yards short of field goal range, and he said a draw play failed when an A-gap blitzer went unaccounted for. He praised Joe Burrow's play and the Bengals' weapons, and he was glowing about safety Amani Hooker. He said a recurring issue with holding penalties on kickoffs needs fixing. Saleh said the team practiced well after trading Jeffery Simmons, and that someone has to step up. He also said the bye should help a banged-up group, with Jacksonville next after the break.

injuries.detail: Dealt with an ankle injury on the last touchdown drive. The team will evaluate him again tomorrow.
